newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks up 3.43pct on strong buying interest.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks up 3.43pct on strong buying interest.

text.p: Greek stocks were trading 3.43 percent higher with construction shares leading the rally and market analysts expected Thursday to be a day of strong buying interest.
"Thursday will be the opposite day of Monday. Instead of panic selling, we will have panic buying," said John Tegopoulos, a chief analyst at Midland-Pandelakis Securities.
He expressed concerns, however, about the market's large recent fluctuations.

"The market is very volatile. On Wednesday shares of construction and banks were trading close to their upper limits. It is the first time we see such strong market movements, and they are scaring long-term conservative funds away," he said.

Market expectations on Athens' strong possibility to be among the four or five candidate cities to host the Olympic Games of 2004 drove construction shares up 3.69 percent 50 minutes into the session. Banking shares were trading 4.87 percent higher.
The Athens general share index was trading 3.43 percent or 44.27 points higher at 1336.44 points from Wednesday's 1292.17, after opening at 1300.41.
Turnover was 10.7 billion drachmas on volume of 2.5 million shares, 50 minutes into the session.

The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 976.00-1014.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, were trading 125 drachmas higher at 5,795.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $42.18-$43.88. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The recently issued ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 1,617-1,796 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 11,685-12,299 drachmas.
